verdicts.reason: A keeps a sensible order: logo, a large headline, bullets, then the CTA. But the bullets are out of sequence (bubbles/herbs/honey reversed), the grocer footer sits in the middle of the list, the bullet indents drift to the right and the first bullet is bigger than the rest. The right half, with the can and circle, is detached from the copy. B is worse: the CTA sits at the top above the headline, the headline and bullets lie on top of the pink circle, the logo is blown up into a huge black pill at the bottom, the list has the same out-of-order and inserted-footer problems, and there is a big dead area at the bottom left.

A has the CTA above the headline, text colliding with the pink circle, a hugely oversized logo pill at the bottom and a jumbled bullet list with the footer inserted in it. That puts it at the bottom of the range, with B ahead. B has a sound centred top-to-bottom order (logo, can, headline, copy, CTA) and keeps the logo and CTA in proportion. But the bullets are still out of order, the footer line sits in the middle of the list, the bullet column is ragged and off-centre, the product is small, and the pink circles float as unrelated decoration.
